{"candidate_slot":0,"current_prompt":"You are given JSON with 'system_profile' (installed products with versions) and 'advisories' (CVEs with 'id', 'description', 'affected'). Determine which advisories affect software actually installed, and return ONLY {"applicable_cves":["CVE-..."]} with unique applicable IDs (or empty array).

PROCEDURE — follow exactly:

STEP 1: PRODUCT MATCHING (be generous; most name differences are aliases of the SAME product).
For each advisory, extract the product from 'affected' (vendor/product). Compare against inventory names after NORMALIZING both: lowercase, replace every '-', '_', '/', '.', '@' with a space, collapse spaces. Matches include:
- Delimiter differences: 'netapp/snapcenter' = 'netapp-snapcenter' = 'netapp snapcenter'; 'usta/aybs' = 'usta-aybs' = 'aybs'; 'phpgurukul/job_portal' = 'phpgurukul job portal'.
- Vendor prefix dropped/added: advisory 'usta/aybs' matches installed 'aybs'; 'dexma/dexgate' matches 'dexgate' or 'dexma-dexgate'. So compare whole normalized strings AND compare after stripping the advisory's vendor portion (just the product part).
- Underscores become spaces: 'esp_hr_management' = 'esp hr management'; 'online_invoicing_system' = 'online invoicing system'.
- Case/punctuation irrelevant: 'Gnome Libsoup' = 'gnome/libsoup'; 'e-belediye' = 'eBelediye'; 'sun.net/ehrd_ctms' = 'sun.net ehrd ctms'; 'm-files/m-files_server' = 'm files m files server'.
- Package-manager names ('oscommerce-oscommerce', 'jetbrains-teamcity', 'sap-solution-manager', 'dell-powerprotect-data-manager', 'opentext-arcsight-intelligence', 'sun.net-ehrd-ctms') match the corresponding advisory products.
- Multi-part advisory products like 'dolibarr/dolibarr_erp/crm' normalize to 'dolibarr dolibarr erp crm'; match if the advisory product (or its product portion) equals/aliases an installed product.
Only reject when products are GENUINELY different software (e.g., 'jetbrains/hub' vs 'jetbrains/teamcity' vs 'jetbrains/youtrack'; 'nozominetworks/cmc' vs 'nozominetworks/guardian'). If an advisory lists several distinct products (OR ranges), it applies if ANY of them is installed.

STEP 2: VERSION PARSING. Parse versions as ordered lists of numeric segments; compare segment by segment NUMERICALLY (never lexicographically: 10.0 > 9.9, 4.10 > 4.9, 20230607 is one segment). Leading zeros irrelevant.
Trailing-segment rule: if the installed version has extra trailing segments vs the bound: if ALL extra segments are 0, the versions are EQUAL (8.31.0.0 = 8.31.0; 6.6.244.0 = 6.6.244; 2024.2.34646.0 = 2024.2.34646; 2.6 = 2.6.0 = 2.6.0.0; 720 = 720.0; 20130114 = 20130114.0). If any extra trailing segment is nonzero, installed is GREATER (4.12.56861 > 4.12.56860; 22.6.3.0 > 22.6.2; 1.0.3.1 > 1.0.3; 2.6.1 > 2.6; 5.10.0.1 > 5.10.0; 8.11.1.1 > 8.11.1; 10.10 > 10.8; 23.11.13156.0.1 > 23.11.13156.0).
A single-segment version (e.g., 9, 720, 20230914) is just that number: installed 9 < bound 20230904; installed 720 = 720.
If the same product appears with multiple installed versions, the advisory applies if ANY version falls in range.

STEP 3: BOUND SEMANTICS — apply the operators in 'affected' EXACTLY:
- 'version < X': affected iff installed < X (strictly). Installed version slightly below X IS affected (22.6.1 < 22.6.2 → affected; 19.14 < 19.15; 4.7 with '>= 3.0 and < 4.9' → affected; 10.0.0.0 < 10.8 → affected).
- 'version <= X': affected iff installed <= X; installed EQUAL to X IS affected (19.15 with '<= 19.15' → affected; 5.5.3 with '<= 5.5.3' → affected; 6.4.2 with '< 6.4.13' → affected).
- 'version >= A and < B' / 'from A before B': installed >= A AND installed < B. Equal to A → affected; equal to B → NOT affected.
- 'version >= A and <= B' / 'A through B': both endpoints included (8.6.0 <= v <= 8.6.5 includes both).
- 'version = X': affected iff numerically equal after trailing-zero normalization (installed 1.0 with '= 1.0' → affected; 7.15.0 with '= 7.15' → affected; 4.0.1.0 with '= 4.0.1' → affected; 4.12.56860.1 with '= 4.12.56860' → NOT affected, since extra segment nonzero makes it greater).
- 'versions prior to X' / 'before X' means installed < X.
- 'versions X and prior' means installed <= X.
- Multiple ranges joined by 'OR': applies if ANY range matches (e.g., 'sap/abap_platform: version = 751 OR ... OR version = 754 OR ...' applies when installed version equals any listed value; installed 754.0 with a bound '754' IS affected).

STEP 4: BOUNDARY CHECKLIST (these decide most cases):
- Installed exactly AT an INCLUSIVE bound (<= B, >= A, = X, or A) → AFFECTED.
- Installed exactly AT an EXCLUSIVE upper bound (< B) → NOT affected (installed 8.31.0.0 with '< 8.31.0' → not affected; 2023.12.0 with '< 2023.12.0' → not; 8.11.1.1 with '< 8.11.1' or '< 8.11' → not; 4.1.0 with '< 4.1.0' → not; 9.1.6.0 with '< 9.1.6' → not; 2.15.0.0 with '< 2.15.0' → not).
- Installed BELOW the fix version → AFFECTED (2023.1.2 < 2023.1.16597 → affected; 1.21 < 1.22 → affected; 6.4.2 < 6.4.13 → affected; 2023.1.16597.1 < 2024.3.52635 → affected).
- Installed ABOVE the upper bound → NOT affected.
- Version equal to the lower bound of a range → affected if below the exclusive upper end.

STEP 5: Do NOT include advisories whose product is not installed under any alias, even if the description mentions other software; do not infer applicability from description text alone. But whenever the product IS installed (under any alias/format) AND its version falls inside the stated range (including inclusive boundaries and equality after trailing-zero normalization), you MUST include that advisory. Systematically check EVERY advisory against EVERY inventory entry; do not stop early.

STEP 6: OUTPUT. Return only valid JSON: {"applicable_cves":[...]} with each ID exactly as supplied, no duplicates, no explanations, no markdown. Empty array only if truly nothing
